_comment: Experience budgets for the Electron desktop app (apps/desktop). Perceived latency only. See README.md in this directory for the status vocabulary and the year-3 volume table. Ratcheted tighten-only via PERF_BUDGET_SOURCES.

coldOpenToUsable.volume: empty (mock-gateway e2e fixture, 1 app, fresh userData) — NOT year-3
coldOpenToUsable.probe: apps/desktop/tests/e2e/launch-time.spec.ts — REAL Electron launch (_electron.launch → firstWindow → Home library visible), nightly desktop-e2e job. Publishes artifacts/perf-input/desktop-launch-report.json, gated by tests/perf/desktop-launch.perf.test.ts.

_provenance.breakdown: process → first window 4494 ms; first window → usable Home 46 ms
_provenance.note: MEASURED, ONE SAMPLE, and NOT re-run since #883 C5 cut the term below — this 4540 ms stands as the last real Electron launch on the record, so the ceiling stays where it is until a fresh launch-time.spec.ts artifact justifies moving it. The headline finding: 99% of the 4.5 s a vault owner waits is MAIN-PROCESS boot before any window exists — the renderer reaches a usable Home 46 ms after it appears. That main-process term is instrumented continuously by the `desktop-cold` rig (tests/perf/desktop-cold.perf.test.ts, budget in tests/quality-rig-budgets.json), which imports the REAL main-process graph in a child process with `electron` stubbed. C1 measured it at 752-855 ms across 1,001 modules on a linux x64 container; before #883 the rig imported gateway-supervisor-core.ts, a file with ZERO imports, so it timed one module parse (~64 ms) and could not have moved if that graph doubled. #883 C5 then attacked the graph itself: three main-process modules were pulling the entire @centraid/server barrel (900 modules, ~770 ms of cold import on its own) — gateway-paths.ts for one path resolver, detached-gateway.ts for one HMAC helper, and embedded-gateway.ts for serve(). The first two now import narrow @centraid/server subpath exports; embedded-gateway.js became a DYNAMIC import inside local-gateway.ts's startEmbedded, which a production launch never reaches (the embedded gateway is selected by CENTRAID_EMBEDDED_GATEWAY=1, for tests — production spawns a DETACHED gateway child). On the same contended container the rig fell from 952-1105 ms / 1,003 modules to 396-431 ms / 430-431 modules, and the main entry's full direct dependency set from 1,034 modules / 815 ms to 461 / 365 ms; the rig budget was ratcheted 3000 -> 1300 ms to match. What is left is dominated by the @centraid/vault barrel (296 modules) that gateway-secrets.ts needs for KeyStore. None of this covers Electron's own runtime start, V8 snapshot restore or window creation, which is why this Playwright ceiling remains the cold-start budget and why the ~450 ms of import cost removed is a floor on, not a measure of, what a vault owner will feel. TIGHTEN this ceiling once ~10 nightly launch samples exist. The sustained-drift gate (30 samples, 1.5x) is what actually catches a slow walk.

tapToVisualResponse.probe: apps/desktop/tests/e2e/launch-time.spec.ts — click an app tile → the app view attaches.

_provenance.host: darwin arm64, same run as coldOpenToUsable
_provenance.note: MEASURED, ONE SAMPLE. Two seconds from clicking a tile to the app view attaching is a long time to look at an unchanged screen, and nothing measured it before. The number includes the app-view mount and its first gateway round trips against the mock gateway. Ceiling ~3x observed, single-sample; tighten on real distribution.

sendToFirstToken.volume: n/a — the desktop e2e mock gateway has no model provider
sendToFirstToken.probe: NONE TODAY. Needs the mock gateway in apps/desktop/tests/e2e/fixtures.ts to serve a fixed-delay SSE turn so the number is the shell's dead time, not a provider's.

maxDroppedFramePercent.probe: NONE TODAY. Chromium exposes no per-frame drop counter to Playwright without a CDP trace; the mobile surface owns the frame-drop ceiling (see mobile.json).

reconnectToFresh.probe: NONE TODAY. Wants a mock-gateway pause/resume in the desktop e2e harness plus a client-side 'data is fresh' signal to observe.
reconnectToFresh._note: #883 C1 measured the same verb on the two surfaces where a probe was cheap — the gateway's side over real HTTP (60 ms, gateway.json) and the phone's client-side resume term (6.3-8.4 s, mobile.json) — and deliberately did NOT flip this entry. The mobile probe drives createNativeReplicaSession, which owns its store, pull loop and change apply in-process; the desktop shell's equivalent is ReplicaShellSession over a coordinator that runs the sqlite-wasm store in a Worker, and packages/client/src/replica/shell-session.test.ts fakes that coordinator wholesale. A probe against the fake would time the mock, not the resume. Landing a number here needs either the real worker-backed coordinator under jsdom or the desktop e2e harness above — neither is a cheap add, and a plausible number with no run behind it is the failure `unmeasured` exists to prevent.

appWeight.volume: n/a — build artifact, independent of vault size
appWeight.probe: scripts/perf/app-weight.mjs --surface desktop (weighs apps/desktop/dist/renderer), run in CI after the desktop build

_provenance.host: darwin arm64, worktree `vite build` output of apps/desktop
_provenance.note: MEASURED by `node scripts/perf/app-weight.mjs --surface desktop --report`. Source maps (10.7 MB of them) are excluded as diagnostics, not product weight. Ceilings are observed + ~8% headroom. The three next-largest shipped files are react-pdf.worker.min.mjs (1.30 MB), sqlite3.wasm (865 kB) and react-boot.css (530 kB) — react-boot.js and react-pdf are both code-split candidates, and when either lands these numbers must be re-measured and TIGHTENED.
